messages:
suresh: Heads up — seeing weird TTFT regression on FP8 prefill for long-context (>16k) runs after the recent hybrid-4bit kernel landing.
marta: which job/benchmark? link pls
suresh: perf-run: `./bench --model redwood-13b-hybrid --mode prefill --seq 32768 --batch 8 --quant fp8+4bit` logs attached below
kevin: can you paste the top-level numbers? tps / ttft / p95
suresh: tps: 18 -> expected ~24, ttft: 210ms -> used to be ~140ms, p95 spiked a lot. CPU side shows dequant hot loop thrashing.
noah: @suresh did we fall back to generic GEMM on some kernels? I think I saw fallback in the logs
suresh: yes: kernel selector warned: "no optimized 4bit-pack kernel for seq>2048, falling back to unpack->gemm". That's likely the culprit.
elaine: that's odd, that fallback should only trigger for certain tile sizes. We changed the tile-heuristic in the hybrid PR. cc @kevin
kevin: can we repro with smaller seq to isolate prefill vs decode? Try seq=4096 and seq=8192
suresh: ran quick: seq=4096 tps=23 ttft=145ms; seq=8192 tps=21 ttft=160ms; so slope steepens after 8k. looks like kernel choice boundary.
perf-bot: [auto-profile] 1766504335 - flamegraph generated: /perf/artifacts/1766504335-flame.svg
marta: flamegraph shows heavy `dequant_pack_unroll` at prefill stage for long ctx
suresh: also KV cache hits unchanged, so not a cache policy issue. This is pure compute kernel path.
noah: calibration questions: did calibration quant params change distribution causing more dynamic range -> slower path?
elaine: calibration stats: mean scale shift 1.02, clip rate +0.2%. Not huge. More likely the packed kernel selection threshold.
kevin: quick mitigation: add temporary kernel alias that uses the smaller tile kernel for seq<=32768 to avoid unpack path. We can test perf impact.
marta: sounds good — also check batching heuristics: when batch=1 decode may pick different kernels. Try batch 4/8/16.
suresh: ran batch sweep on seq=32768: batch4 tps=19, batch8 tps=18, batch16 tps=10 (memory thrash). Batch8 is closest to expected but still low.
noah: curious about TTFT vs TPS tradeoff: our prefill path is latency-bound with large matmuls but decode is token-bound. Are we measuring warm vs cold init?
suresh: warm-run included. Cold init negligible here. Problem appears during sustained prefill matmuls.
elaine: OK action items:
- kevin: add kernel alias + run 1h perf job (seq 32k, batch 8) — due EOD
- marta: validate tile-heuristic change in recent PR and revert if needed
- noah: re-run calibration with more long-context prompts and check quant stats
- suresh: gather full perf artifacts (nvprof/trace/fio) and attach
kevin: starting job now. command: 
``
./bench --model redwood-13b-hybrid --mode prefill --seq 32768 --batch 8 --quant fp8+4bit --kernel-alias=small-tile
```
marta: FYI we should also test INT8 path; if int8 kernels avoid unpack fallback we might prefer a temporary route for Dedicated customers.
suresh: note: customer incident risk low — only internal perf regression so far, but production rollouts tomorrow should be blocked until we confirm.
perf-bot: [status] job 1766504390 finished — tps=23 ttft=148ms for kernel-alias run
noah: great — kernel alias seems to recover TPS. can we keep alias behind a runtime flag for canary?
kevin: yes — will ship as runtime flag and add unit that checks kernel selection boundary
marta: thanks everyone — will open a short postmortem-ish thread once we have TPU/GPU end-to-end numbers. :+1:
suresh: attaching logs and nvprof snippet:
``
# nvprof snippet
==PROF== Kernel: pack4bit_unpack: time 124ms
==PROF== Kernel: gemm_generic: time 312ms
```
elaine: good. closing for now until further artifacts. ping if anything else shows up.
